name: Labubu
blurb: Pop Mart's toothy monster doll, the blind-box bag charm everyone queued for in 2024–25
title: Labubu Meaning: Why Everyone on TikTok Wants One
description: Labubu is a furry, grinning monster toy by artist Kasing Lung, sold by Pop Mart in blind boxes. It became a global craze after Lisa of Blackpink showed one in 2024.
answer: Labubu is a furry little monster with pointed ears and a wide grin full of nine sharp teeth, created by Hong Kong-born artist Kasing Lung for his picture-book series The Monsters in 2015. Chinese toy company Pop Mart has produced Labubu figures since 2019, mostly in blind boxes, so you don't know which design you will get. After Lisa of Blackpink was seen with a Labubu bag charm in April 2024, it spread across Asia and then TikTok worldwide, with sell-out drops, queues and huge resale prices in 2025.

body: Labubu is one character in Kasing Lung's The Monsters, a cast of elf-like creatures drawn from Nordic folklore. Its look is often called "ugly-cute": shaggy fur, rabbit-like ears and a mischievous toothy smile. The best-known products are the plush keychains people clip to their bags, plus vinyl figures in themed series.

body.note: Most Labubus are sold in sealed blind boxes. Each series has several regular designs and a rare "secret" figure, which is a big part of the thrill and of the resale market.

head: Date
Event
rows: Kasing Lung introduces Labubu in The Monsters picture books and figures.
Lung signs a licensing deal with Pop Mart, which launches the first Labubu figures.
Lisa of Blackpink is photographed with a Labubu keychain; demand surges in Thailand and across Southeast Asia.
Pop Mart says The Monsters series brought in more than US$419 million in 2024, up 726.6% on the year before.
The plush series Big Into Energy drops worldwide at the same time; it sells out and resale prices jump.
A life-size mint-green Labubu sells for 1.08 million yuan at an auction in Beijing.
Fakes nicknamed "Lafufu" flood the market; Pop Mart sues 7-Eleven in California over counterfeit toys.
Pop Mart reports third-quarter revenue down 45–50% year on year, with the steepest falls overseas.

ul: Unboxing videos: "Opening six blind boxes, please let me pull the secret one."
Bag styling: "My bag isn't finished until a Labubu is hanging off it."
Spotting fakes: "Count the teeth. A real Labubu has nine, that one is a Lafufu."
Joking about the hype: "I queued three hours for a toy I didn't know existed a month ago."

body: Labubu is still one of the most recognisable collectible toys, but the frenzy has cooled. Pop Mart's sales fell sharply in 2026, especially outside mainland China, and resale prices are far below their 2025 peaks. On TikTok, Labubu is now as likely to appear in jokes about fads as in hauls. It sits in the same family as other viral crazes like Dubai chocolate: a product that turned into a meme.

faq.a: Kasing Lung, a Hong Kong-born artist who grew up in the Netherlands. Pop Mart makes and sells the toys under licence.
A fake Labubu. Counterfeits often have the wrong number of teeth, rougher fur or odd colours, and the nickname became a joke of its own.

faq.q: Why are Labubus sold in blind boxes?
faq.a: You pay for a sealed box without knowing which design is inside, so collectors buy more to complete a set or find the rare secret figure.
